newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Oct 11.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Oct 11.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The September official labour force figures released yesterday show that Australia has hardly created any new jobs in the past 11 months, a figure that reflects the jobs market's continuing frailty and suggests the Reserve Bank may cut short-term interest rates soon. Page 1.

Ministerial standards are at the centre of a political storm for the Federal Government, with Prime Minister John Howard coming close to firing Assistant Treasurer Jim Short for breaching conflict of interest guidelines on company share holdings. Also under fire from the Opposition was Howard's main political adviser Grahame Morris, following the Government awarding a A$1 million contract to DDB Needham which was associated with part of the Liberals 1996 election campaign. Page 3.

Prime Minister John Howard has stated that he will look into reviving the investigation into the dealings of former media and property magnate Christopher Skase after outrage that the pursuit of Skase would end. This decision is a backflip on the Government's earlier decision to drop the investigation's funding. Page 3.

Speakers at a peak manufacturing dinner have slammed the Federal Government for having no vision and showing no leadership on industry policy and cutting programs for manufacturers to spare mining and agricultural interests. Members of the meeting include BHP, Transfield and ANL. Page 4.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Prime Minister John Howard has forced Assistant Treasurer Jim Short to sell his banking shares and donate the profits to charity. Howard told Parliament yesterday that Senator Short had "overlooked" the code of ministerial conduct by failing to divest almost A$50,000 in ANZ Bank shares while he had responsibility for banking and superannuation. Short denied there was any conflict of interest, saying the continuing ownership of the shares was an oversight. Page 1.

Hours after the Insolvency and Trustee Service of Australia (ITSA), within the Attorney-General's Department, decided to quit the investigation aimed at recovering proceeds for investors in Christopher Skase's failed Quintex empire because of spiralling Government costs, Prime Minister John Howard ordered a separate review of the bankruptcy case, to determine whether investigations to recover assets of the self-exiled tycoon should continue. Page 1.

Under reforms being considered by the Australian Tax Office, business would be relieved from the burden of recording every intricate detail which would be considered an exchange for payment in a flat fringe benefit tax. The ATO has proposed a standard formula which could be applied to businesses to alleviate the mountain of paperwork which is associated with the current fringe benefit tax laws. Page 1.

Following the release of the latest unemployment figures which recorded a jobless rate of 8.7 per cent in September, Employment Minister Amanda Vanstone has refused to commit the Government to reducing the jobless rate by the next Federal election. The latest figure shows little change from the August figure of 8.8 per cent unemployed. Page 2.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

A six-year-old boy is fighting for his life after being doused in petrol and set alight at a Queensland school yesterday. Onlookers were shocked when the man walked into the playground of the Cairns school with a can of petrol and set the boy alight with cigarette lighter. After the apparently random attack, the man surrendered himself to police. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard has called for a review of the hunt for failed media tycoon Christopher Skase's wealth, following widespread condemnation of moves to end the assets search. Skase is believed to have left Australia with A$10 million in cash and assets and the Government has spent over A$700,000 in a bid to trace his assets over the past two years. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard admitted in question time yesterday he considered sacking Assistant Treasurer Jim Short after the Opposition revealed he still owned 6,679 ANZ Bank shares, while his portfolio responsibility covered banking policy. The Opposition claims the share ownership was a clear breach of interest with the Minister's duties, as the shares should have been sold six months ago and that by only selling them now he had gained A$9,083. Page 1.

According to a new study of multinational corporations, the New South Wales Government has neglected the battle to win new international business and has shown little interest in dealing with industry. The Economist Group survey found New South Wales lagged well behind Victoria and Queensland in encouraging new business and more than a quarter surveyed believed Carr Government support for foreign industry and investment was "poor". Page 3.
THE AGE

Prime Minister John Howard has decided not to sack his Assistant Treasurer Jim Short for his breach of ministerial guidelines in owning A$48,000 worth of bank shares whilst being responsible for banking policy, Howard announced his main reason for his decision was that he believed Short had not acted with impropriety. Page 1.

Victorian Education Minister Phil Gude told Parliament yesterday that Victoria had 1500 excess teachers who did no work and that these teachers cost the system A$26 million last year and would cost A$20 million in 1996. Gude stated there would be further voluntary redundancies of teachers this year. Page 1.

The head of the Peter MacCallum Cancer Institute said yesterday that the way in which Victoria's case-mix funding was being applied discriminated against patients, stating that he would have to scrap 100 jobs and close a specialty ward to meet a A$4 million budget deficit. Page 1.

Victoria's unemployment figures continue to rise, with the number out of work rising to an 18 month high and increasing at a faster rate than the national average. Victoria now has an unemployment rate of 9.4 per cent, or 214,600 people, a rise since Junes figure of 8.1 per cent. Page 1.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
